signal.mechanism: A contraction of disagreement about next-calendar-year real GDP growth may reduce required compensation for disagreement risk and support equity valuations. This is a deliberately falsifiable slow state hypothesis, not an established directional law; agreement is not subjective uncertainty and information may already be priced.
signal.dispersion: p75 minus p25, in percentage points; zero is valid, inverted or missing quartiles are not
signal.comparison: Current survey target year equals survey calendar year+1. Compare with the immediately previous survey for exactly that same forecast year, including the previous survey's year+2 if crossing a calendar year. No earlier usable-survey fallback and no cross-year forecast comparison.
signal.primary: MIX long0.9 if current IQR strictly below previous IQR and both pairs are valid; otherwise cash. Equal/wider IQR means cash, no short arm.
signal.control: constant MIX long0.9 only on the identical paired-source-readiness/fill calendar; contextual baseline, not promotable after results
signal.availability: 23:59:59 Europe/Moscow on last calendar day of month following survey_month, inherited unchanged. Current retrieval and Last-Modified never backdate availability. Numeric source reader excludes releases available from2026 BEFORE loading values.
signal.source_date: conservative availability's local calendar date for TTL; original survey_month and predecessor clocks retained separately
signal.missing: Missing, nonfinite or inverted selected quartile masks the newest survey and its immediate successor comparison. No older good-state fallback, numerical imputation, participant reconstruction or replacement indicator.

limitations: New distributional information, not V21 median revision signs, channel addition, sign reversal or reweighted forecast composite. Median forecasts are excluded from the numerical read. One predeclared GDP IQR contraction rule and control; no sign/quantile/horizon/threshold/universe/size/expiry/cost tuning after outcomes.

Survey disagreement differs from an individual's predictive uncertainty. Selected literature motivates dispersion as priced information and documents state-dependent, sometimes different signs; it does not validate this Russian index timing rule. Narrowing as horizon approaches, changing respondents and rounding may create the signal without any tradable risk repricing. Counts/individual forecasts unavailable for a constant-participant panel.
